scope: Three finding-specific static correlation reviews. Exact member path, raw byte length, SHA256 and rule are required; original findings remain visible as warnings. No package exemption, execution permission, advisory override, binary clearance or coverage waiver.
evidence: The existing npm cache archives match the desktop package-lock SHA512 integrity. Their SHA256 matches the published dependency scan evidence. Each member was read without extraction or execution and matches the installed local source byte-for-byte.

reviews.reason: The two environment-collection pattern matches are process.env passed to the Yarn PATH-key chooser (line 9) and Object.keys(process.env).filter(/^debug_/i) for debug-formatting options (line 29). The former inspects the environment key spelling; the latter selects debugging keys. Neither match serializes/uploads the environment. The bundle also exposes explicit fetch and filesystem/compiler helpers, which are real build-tool capabilities and are not approved by this correlation review. Network/dynamic-execution findings remain visible and every other rule retains its original handling.

The credential-path regex matches the string cookies in the minifier DOM-property-name table (line 268894), alongside cookie/cookieEnabled/cookieStore. It does not identify a browser cookie database read. Compiler filesystem helpers and module-fetch code are real, independent capabilities; their co-occurrence with that property-name string is not credential-to-network dataflow. This review covers only the exact correlation. Existing credential-file and network/dynamic warnings remain visible; it does not approve compiler plugins, downloads, subprocesses or changed source.

The environment-collection pattern matches stripSensitiveEnvVars(process.env) passed as the child-process environment (line 330). The dependency collector intentionally launches the selected local package-manager dependency-list command with argument arrays and the default shell:false setting; on Windows it uses the documented PowerShell argument-encoding wrapper, then parses its output. The network regex's fetch matches are prose describing dependency-tree collection rather than an HTTP API in this source. This is a reviewed false correlation, not permission to execute package managers or a guarantee about child processes. Credential filtering and every sibling member/rule remain independently inspected.

limitations: Static correlation review, not a general malware audit or proof of package safety.
Every changed byte, path, other rule, decoded/lifecycle payload, advisory, native binary or incomplete coverage keeps its existing handling.
